from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Why does this pencil look broken in water?",
            "Light travels in a straight line usually.",
            "Entering water, the light path actually bends."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The 'Broken' Pencil Mystery", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        glass = Rectangle(height=3, width=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        pencil_top = Line(UP, ORIGIN, color=GRAY)
        pencil_bottom = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN, color=GRAY)
        
        # Initial assembly for pencil
        pencil_group = VGroup(pencil_top, pencil_bottom)
        self.place_at_grid(glass, 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(pencil_group, 'D3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(glass), Create(pencil_top), Create(pencil_bottom))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        light_ray = DashedLine(UP*2 + LEFT*2, DOWN*2 + RIGHT*2, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(light_ray))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        interface = Line(LEFT*0.75, RIGHT*0.75, color="#FFD700").move_to(glass.get_top())
        bend_point = Dot(color="#FF4500").move_to(interface.get_center())
        
        # Show bending
        self.play(Create(interface), FadeIn(bend_point))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Core Principle: Snell's Law", [
            "Snell's Law calculates light refraction angles.",
            "Incident rays meet the normal line.",
            "Light bends toward or away normal.",
            "Math predicts the path very accurately.",
            "Watch the light ray change direction."
        ])

        # Objects
        formula = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin(\theta_1) = n_2 \sin(\theta_2)", color=WHITE)
        normal = DashedLine(start=UP*2, end=DOWN*2, color=LIGHT_GRAY)
        surface = Line(start=LEFT*3, end=RIGHT*3, color=BLUE)
        ray_in = Line(start=LEFT*2+UP*1.5, end=ORIGIN, color=YELLOW)
        ray_out = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5+DOWN*1, color=YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'A3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(surface), FadeIn(normal))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(LIGHT_GRAY)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(ray_in))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Create(ray_out))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Simple movement to show bending
        self.play(ray_out.animate.rotate(-0.5, about_point=ORIGIN))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(RED)

        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Archerfish spot prey above the water.",
            "Refraction distorts the prey's real position.",
            "Fish learn to aim below apparent image."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Nature's Adaptation: The Archerfish", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        water_surface = Line(LEFT*3, RIGHT*3, color=BLUE).shift(DOWN*0.5)
        prey = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid["B3"])
        fish = Dot(color=RED).move_to(self.grid["E3"])
        
        apparent_prey = Dot(color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        
        # Lines
        light_ray_1 = Line(prey.get_center(), self.grid["D2"], color=YELLOW)
        light_ray_2 = Line(self.grid["D2"], fish.get_center(), color=YELLOW)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(water_surface), FadeIn(prey), FadeIn(fish))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(Create(light_ray_1), Create(light_ray_2))
        self.play(FadeIn(apparent_prey))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        aim_line = DashedLine(fish.get_center(), self.grid["D3"], color=RED)
        self.play(Create(aim_line))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Physics of Light: Understanding Refraction

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Broken' Pencil Mystery
sections.content: Hook the audience with a visual demonstration of a pencil appearing broken when placed in a glass of water. Introduce the concept that light doesn't always travel in straight lines.
sections.example: A pencil submerged in a glass of water appears offset at the surface; we explain this as light 'bending' when crossing media boundaries.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Speed of Light and Optical Density
sections.content: Establish that light travels fastest in a vacuum and slows down when moving through denser materials (like water or glass). Define 'Refractive Index' (n) as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed in the medium.
sections.example: Visualize light as a 'marching line of soldiers' moving from a smooth pavement (air) into thick mud (water), causing them to slow down and change direction.

sections.title: Core Principle: Snell's Law
sections.content: Present Snell's Law (n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2)). Use a graphical split-screen: show the incident ray, the normal line, and the refracted ray. Animate the angles changing as the refractive index changes.
sections.example: A laser beam hitting a glass block at an angle: display the calculated math on one side of the screen while the animation shows the ray bending toward the 'normal' line.

sections.title: Nature's Adaptation: The Archerfish
sections.content: Apply the theory to the Archerfish, which spits water at insects above the surface. Explain that the fish must compensate for the refraction of light to accurately aim at its prey.
sections.example: An animation showing the Archerfish looking at an insect: the fish sees the 'apparent' position (refracted image) and aims slightly below where the prey appears to be.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: Light slows down in denser media, causing it to bend toward the normal. This governs everything from the human eye's lens to fiber-optic cables in global communications.
sections.example: A fast-paced montage: a lens focusing light onto a retina, a diamond sparkling due to internal refraction, and an fiber-optic pulse carrying high-speed internet.
